title: Momotaro
levelRationale: N5-oriented polite retelling in eight sections, about 1,000-1,500 characters, using です/ます, て-form requests, たい, and reason から. It is a learning target, not an official JLPT certification. Story exceptions are reported in the source record: the name 桃太郎 uses the N1 kanji 桃; 鬼 and 宝 are N3; 島 is N4; kana むかし links to the N4 card 昔; さる links to the N3 card 猿; だんご and きじ have no card. The fruit is written もも. 空から and 家から mark a source, not a reason. The peach evaluation, the oni's badness, the dog's request, and the oni's weakness are authored causes in this wording, not claims about every traditional version. Questions include the quote they test, or ask about a cause the passage states, so either quiz mode can be fair.

sections.text: むかし、小さい村におじいさんとおばあさんがいました。おじいさんは毎日山へ行きました。山で仕事をしました。おばあさんは毎日川へ行きました。そして二人は家へ帰りました。家でご飯を食べました。夜、二人は家で話しました。
sections.translation: Long ago, an old man and an old woman lived in a small village. Every day the old man went to the mountain and worked there. Every day the old woman went to the river. Then the two of them returned home, ate a meal, and talked at night.

sections.text: ある日、おばあさんは川で大きいももを見ました。ももは水の上にありました。おばあさんは「いいももです」と言いました。いいももですから、ももを家へ持ちました。家で、ももを置きました。おじいさんも大きいももを見ました。
sections.translation: One day, the old woman saw a large peach at the river. The peach was on the water. She said, "It is a good peach." Because it was a good peach, she took it home. She put it down, and the old man saw it too.

sections.text: 家で、おじいさんとおばあさんはももを切りました。ももの中から男の子が出ました。男の子は小さい子供でした。二人は「だれですか」と言いました。男の子は二人を見ました。二人は「いい子供です」と言いました。
sections.translation: At home, the old man and woman cut the peach. A boy came out of it. He was a small child. They asked, "Who are you?" The boy looked at them, and they said, "He is a good child."

sections.text: 二人は「この子供の名前は桃太郎です」と言いました。桃太郎は小さい子供でした。桃太郎は毎日ご飯をたくさん食べました。桃太郎はおじいさんと山へ歩きました。桃太郎は山で仕事をしました。そして強い子供になりました。
sections.translation: They said, "This child's name is Momotaro." He was a small child. Every day he ate a lot of meals, walked to the mountain with the old man, and worked there. Then he became a strong child.

sections.text: 桃太郎は村で人の話を聞きました。村の人は言いました。「悪い鬼が島にいます。鬼は毎日村の物を取ります。」桃太郎はおじいさんとおばあさんに言いました。「鬼は悪いですから、私は島へ行きたいです。」二人は「行ってください」と言いました。二人は島へ行きませんでした。
sections.translation: Momotaro heard what people in the village said. They said, "A bad oni is on the island. Every day the oni takes the village's things." Momotaro said to the old man and woman, "Because the oni is bad, I want to go to the island." They said, "Please go." They did not go to the island.

sections.text: 朝、おばあさんはだんごをたくさん作りました。桃太郎に「これを持ってください」と言いました。おばあさんは「道で一つ食べてください」と言いました。桃太郎は「はい」と言いました。桃太郎はだんごを持ちました。そして家を出ました。
sections.translation: In the morning, the old woman made many dumplings. She said to Momotaro, "Please take these," and, "Please eat one on the road." He said, "Yes," took the dumplings, and then left home.

sections.text: 島へ行く道で、桃太郎はだんごを一つ食べました。それから、犬が来ました。「どこへ行きますか」と聞きました。桃太郎は「島へ行きます。悪い鬼がいます」と言いました。犬は「だんごをください。私も行きます」と言いましたから、桃太郎は犬にだんごを一つ出しました。それから、さるが来ました。さるも「だんごをください。私も行きます」と言いました。桃太郎はさるにもだんごを一つ出しました。桃太郎は空を見ました。きじは空から来ました。きじは「私も行きたいです」と言いました。桃太郎はきじにもだんごを一つ出しました。桃太郎はだんごを出しましたから、犬とさるときじと一緒に島へ行きました。
sections.translation: On the road to the island, Momotaro ate one dumpling. After that, a dog came and asked, "Where are you going?" Momotaro said, "I am going to the island. A bad oni is there." Because the dog said, "Please give me a dumpling. I will go too," Momotaro gave him one. After that, a monkey came and said, "Please give me a dumpling. I will go too," and Momotaro gave him one too. Momotaro looked at the sky. A pheasant came from the sky and said, "I want to go too." Momotaro gave the pheasant one dumpling too. Because he had given out dumplings, he went to the island with the dog, the monkey, and the pheasant.

sections.text: 島で、桃太郎と犬とさるときじは歩きました。鬼の家がありました。鬼は家から出ました。鬼は桃太郎と犬とさるときじを見ました。鬼は弱いですから、宝を出しました。「この宝を持ってください」と言いました。桃太郎と犬とさるときじは宝を持ちました。そして村へ歩きました。おじいさんとおばあさんは家で待ちました。二人は「これは何ですか」と言いました。桃太郎は「この宝は島の宝です」と言いました。桃太郎と犬とさるときじは家で宝を置きました。鬼は島にいました。
sections.translation: On the island, Momotaro, the dog, the monkey, and the pheasant walked. The oni's house was there. The oni came out of the house and saw them. Because the oni was weak, he took out treasure and said, "Please take this treasure." They carried it and walked to the village. The old man and woman waited at home. They asked, "What is this?" Momotaro said, "This treasure is the island's treasure." Momotaro, the dog, the monkey, and the pheasant put the treasure down at home. The oni was still on the island.

questions.prompt: Where did the old woman see the peach?

options.text: At the river
On the mountain
Inside the house

questions.explanation: She saw the large peach at the river. The old man went to the mountain, and the peach was cut at home later.

questions.prompt: What came out of the peach?

options.text: A boy
A dog
Treasure

questions.explanation: A boy came out from inside the peach. The dog and the treasure appear later.

questions.prompt: What did the old woman make in the morning?

options.text: Dumplings
A peach
Treasure

questions.explanation: In the morning she made many dumplings. The peach was found earlier, and the treasure appears on the island.

questions.prompt: Where did the pheasant come from?

options.text: From the sky
From the river
From the oni's house

questions.explanation: The pheasant came from the sky. The peach was at the river, and the oni came out of his house.

questions.prompt: What happened first?

options.text: The old woman saw a peach at the river
A boy came out of the peach
Momotaro went to the island

questions.explanation: She saw the peach before they cut it and before Momotaro went to the island.

questions.prompt: The old woman says 「これを持ってください」. What is これ?

options.text: The dumplings she made
The peach from the river
The treasure

questions.explanation: She made dumplings and then told Momotaro to take them. これ refers to those dumplings, not the peach or the treasure.

questions.prompt: On the road to the island, who came first?

options.text: The dog
The monkey
The pheasant

questions.explanation: The dog came first. After that the monkey came, and the pheasant came from the sky later.

questions.prompt: The old man and woman ask 「これは何ですか」. What are they asking about?

options.text: The treasure Momotaro brought from the island
The peach from the river
The dumpling Momotaro ate on the road

questions.explanation: They ask after the treasure has been carried to the village. Momotaro answers that this treasure is the island's treasure.

questions.prompt: Why did the old woman take the peach home?

options.text: Because it was a good peach
Because the oni asked her to take it
Because the peach was the treasure

questions.explanation: The story states the reason: it was a good peach, so she took it home. It does not say the oni asked, and the treasure appears later.

questions.prompt: Why did Momotaro want to go to the island?

options.text: Because the oni is bad
Because the old man ordered the animals to go
Because Momotaro already had the treasure

questions.explanation: He states the reason: the oni is bad, so he wants to go. The story does not say the old man ordered the animals, and the treasure comes later.

questions.prompt: Why did Momotaro give the dog a dumpling?

options.text: Because the dog asked for a dumpling
Because the dog was weak
Because the old woman was on the road

questions.explanation: The story states the reason: the dog said please give me a dumpling, so Momotaro gave him one. It does not say the dog was weak or that the old woman was there.

questions.prompt: Why did the dog, monkey, and pheasant go to the island with Momotaro?

options.text: Because he had given out dumplings
Because the old man ordered the animals to go
Because they already had the treasure

questions.explanation: The passage says he had given out dumplings, so he went to the island with the dog, the monkey, and the pheasant. Earlier sentences show one dumpling for each animal. It does not say the old man ordered them or that they already had the treasure.

questions.prompt: Why did the oni take out the treasure?

options.text: Because he was weak
Because Momotaro gave him a dumpling
Because the old woman asked him

questions.explanation: The story gives the cause directly: the oni was weak, so he took out the treasure. The old woman was waiting at home.

questions.prompt: Which statement fits the whole story?

options.text: Momotaro leaves home with dumplings, meets the animals on the road, reaches the island once, and the treasure is put at home
Momotaro stays at the river and never goes to the island
The oni comes to the village at the beginning and gives Momotaro a peach

questions.explanation: He leaves home, the animals meet him on the road, they reach the island once, and the treasure is put down at home. The other statements contradict that order.

questions.prompt: Which statement fits the people who do not travel to the island, and the oni at the end?

options.text: The old man and woman do not go to the island and wait at home. At the end the oni is still on the island
The old man goes to the island every day instead of the mountain
The oni comes to the house and waits there with the grandparents

questions.explanation: They tell Momotaro to go, but they do not go, and they wait at home. The last sentence says the oni was on the island.

questions.prompt: What happens to the dumplings across the story?

options.text: The old woman makes them, Momotaro eats one on the road, and he gives one each to the dog, the monkey, and the pheasant
The oni eats the dumplings and then gives Momotaro the treasure
The old man and woman take the dumplings to the island

questions.explanation: She makes them at home, he eats one on the road, and he gives one to each animal before they reach the island. The oni is not given a dumpling, and the grandparents do not go.

questions.prompt: Where does the treasure end up, and who brings it there?

options.text: The oni takes it out on the island. Momotaro and the animals carry it to the village and put it at home
It stays in the oni's house
The old woman finds it in the river at the beginning

questions.explanation: The oni takes the treasure out, the party carries it to the village, and it is put down at home. It is not left in the oni's house, and the river object was a peach.

questions.prompt: What do the village people say the oni does every day?

options.text: He takes the village's things
He makes dumplings
He waits at Momotaro's house

questions.explanation: They say the oni takes the village's things every day. The old woman makes the dumplings, and the old man and woman wait at home.

questions.prompt: On the road, what did Momotaro do before the dog came?

options.text: He ate one dumpling
He gave a dumpling to the pheasant
He put the treasure at home

questions.explanation: He ate one dumpling, and after that the dog came. The pheasant comes later, and the treasure is put down at home after the island.

questions.prompt: Which statement fits Momotaro before he leaves home?

options.text: He was a small child, ate many meals, worked on the mountain, and became strong. Then he said he wanted to go to the island
He was already strong at the beginning and never ate
The oni became strong, and Momotaro stayed a small child

questions.explanation: The name section says he was small, ate a lot, worked on the mountain, and became strong. In the next section he says he wants to go. He leaves home after that. The passage does not say the oni became strong.
